chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Acquire deep understanding in the religion, for indeed whoever among you does not acquire deep understanding in the religion is a Bedouin.'
Indeed, Allah says in His Book: 'that they may acquire deep understanding in religion, and that they may warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious.'

key_terms.أَعْرَابِيٌّ: Bedouin, Arab nomad — used in the Quran (49:14) to describe those whose faith has not yet entered their hearts; here a metaphor for religious ignorance
key_terms.تَفَقَّهُوا: Acquire deep religious understanding (tafaqquh) — from fiqh, meaning not merely knowledge but penetrating comprehension of religious law and principles
key_terms.لِيُنْذِرُوا: That they may warn/admonish — the duty to convey religious knowledge and caution to one's community

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the obligation of acquiring deep understanding in religion?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) commands his followers to acquire deep religious understanding (tafaqquh), warning that one who neglects this becomes like an illiterate Bedouin — spiritually disconnected from the faith. He grounds this command in Quran 9:122, which prescribes a division of labor in the community: some stay to learn religion deeply so that upon returning they may warn their communities. The comparison to a 'Bedouin' (a'rabi) would have resonated strongly with early Muslim audiences, as Bedouins were often depicted in the Quran as having superficial or no real faith.
word_analysis: that they may acquire deep understanding
